mainTopic: Why רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון argue about a partly-severed limb, and questions about when a יד connects things in different states
overview: The amud opens by finishing a source where רבי מאיר seems to require that the big piece rise with the small one before they count as connected. This clashes with his view in our משנה. רבי יוחנן answers that the names in that source are switched. The גמרא asks whether טבול יום might simply be different, brings רבי's ברייתא that all טומאות are the same here, and then concludes that the switch is needed only according to רבי. Next, a series of אמוראים each explain the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון in a new way: רבא (a יד for הכשר), רב פפא (הכשר before מחשבה, proven from רבי עקיבא's change of mind about village fat), רב אחא בריה דרב איקא (blood wiped off between the סימנים), and רב אשי (the שחיטה itself gives הכשר, not the blood). רבה then asks whether a living animal can be a יד for its limb, and אביי asks whether part of a cucumber growing out of its pot can be a יד for the rest; both questions end in תיקו. Finally רבי ירמיה quotes the rule that bowing to half a gourd forbids that half, and begins a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's lifting test for a partly-attached piece
steps.stepSummary: The quoted source ends with רבי מאיר's rule: if lifting the small piece lifts the big piece too, they count as one; if not, they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: If you hold the small piece and the big piece comes up with it, then it counts as the same item. If not, it does not count as the same item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from another source, where רבי מאיר gives a lifting test for whether two attached pieces count as one. This quote is the basis of a contradiction the גמרא is raising against רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is about food that is partly broken but still slightly attached, where someone impure touches the small piece. Here רבי מאיר says the pieces count as one only if the big piece rises when you lift the small one. That clashes with רבי מאיר in our משנה, who treats a partly-severed limb as part of the animal even without this test.

keyTerms.meaning: holds, grasps
the small piece / the big piece
comes up together with it when lifted
like it, counted as the same item

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not start a new topic. It is the end of a quote the גמרא brought to point out a contradiction in רבי מאיר's views.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
If one holds the small piece
and the big piece comes up with it,
then it is counted as the same as it;
and if not, it is not counted as the same as it.
phrases.notes: Here 'the same' means the two pieces count as one item, so impurity spreads from one to the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי מאיר אומר: אם אוחז בקטן וגדול עולה עמו
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's view in the משנה that a partly-severed limb counts as part of the animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the other source רבי מאיר requires that the big piece rise with the small one. That suggests he would not treat a loosely-hanging limb as connected, which contradicts his view in our משנה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the names are switched
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן solves the contradiction by saying the opinions in the other source were assigned to the wrong sages.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: The opinions are switched.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the contradiction. He says that in that other source the names should be reversed, so the lifting test is not really רבי מאיר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the names are swapped, רבי מאיר holds that the pieces count as one even if the big piece does not rise. That fits his view in our משנה, so the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: switched, reversed
the line-up of opinions, who said what
the opinions were assigned to the wrong sages and must be swapped

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The opinions are switched.
phrases.notes: He means that in that other source, רבי מאיר's name and the other sage's name should trade places.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואמר רבי יוחנן: מוחלפת השיטה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching the names in the source (reversed attribution)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lifting test belongs to רבי מאיר, which clashes with our משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: The lifting test belongs to the other sage. רבי מאיר holds the pieces are connected even without it, which matches our משנה.

steps.title: Why is it a contradiction? Maybe טבול יום is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the two statements clash at all, since רבי מאיר might treat a טבול יום more leniently than other kinds of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the problem? Maybe רבי מאיר makes a difference between a טבול יום and other kinds of impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back and questions whether there was ever a real contradiction. It suggests a simple way to make both statements of רבי מאיר fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other source is about a טבול יום, someone who already went to the מקוה and only waits for nightfall. That is a weaker kind of טומאה, so רבי מאיר might be more lenient there and count the pieces as connected only if the big piece rises. If so, there would be no need to swap the names.

keyTerms.meaning: and what is the difficulty? (questioning whether a problem really exists)
maybe, perhaps
he distinguishes, it is different for him
someone who immersed today and is waiting for nightfall to become fully pure

phrases.english: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps Rabbi Meir distinguishes
between one who immersed that day and other kinds of impurity.
phrases.notes: The other source was about a טבול יום, while our משנה is about regular טומאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: ומאי קושיא? דילמא שני ליה לרבי מאיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבי יוחנן's name-switch was needed at all
steps.kashyaTarget: The basic contradiction from step 1, and so the need for רבי יוחנן's answer in step 2
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two statements of רבי מאיר are about different kinds of טומאה. He could simply treat טבול יום more leniently, so there is no real clash.

steps.title: רבי: טבול יום and other impurities are the same
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי says טבול יום and other kinds of טומאה follow the same rules, so the suggested difference fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי says: Both a טבול יום and other kinds of impurity are the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by quoting a ברייתא. It shows that we cannot treat טבול יום differently here, so the contradiction is real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי teaches that what counts as connected for one kind of טומאה counts the same way for every kind. So רבי מאיר cannot have one rule for טבול יום and another for regular טומאה. The contradiction stands, and רבי יוחנן's name-switch is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: both this and that, the same rule applies to each
all other kinds of impurity
a teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי holds that the rules of connection are the same for טבול יום and for all other טומאה. Step 5 will ask whether רבי מאיר must agree, and step 6 limits רבי יוחנן's switch to רבי's view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the rules about when two pieces count as one item are the same for every kind of טומאה.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rebbi says:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד טְבוּל יוֹם וְאֶחָד שְׁאָר טוּמְאוֹת.
phrases.english: Both one who immersed that day and other kinds of impurity are the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: תניא, רבי אומר: אחד טבול יום ואחד שאר טומאות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 3 and confirms the contradiction is real
steps.raayaObject: That טבול יום and other kinds of טומאה cannot be treated differently for these rules
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי: אחד טבול יום ואחד שאר טומאות

steps.title: Maybe רבי and רבי מאיר disagree about טבול יום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי's ברייתא doesn't prove anything about רבי מאיר, since רבי מאיר may still treat a טבול יום differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe for רבי there is no difference, and for רבי מאיר there is a difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from step 4. Just because רבי treats טבול יום like other טומאה does not mean רבי מאיר agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 used רבי's ברייתא to say there is no difference between a טבול יום and other טומאה. But that is only רבי's view. רבי מאיר could still hold that a טבול יום is more lenient, and then his two rulings would not contradict each other at all.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference for him; he makes a distinction
But perhaps (introduces a possible way out)

phrases.english: But perhaps for רבי there is no difference,
phrases.notes: He means no difference between a טבול יום and other kinds of טומאה, like the ברייתא in step 4 said.

phrases.english: and for רבי מאיר there is a difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא, לְרַבִּי לָא שָׁנֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 4 by limiting it to רבי alone.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of רבי's ברייתא to prove that רבי מאיר makes no distinction for a טבול יום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One תנא's view cannot be assumed for another תנא; רבי מאיר may still hold a different view.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's swap was only according to רבי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה explains that רבי יוחנן said the opinions are switched only according to רבי's approach.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יאשיה said: This is what רבי יוחנן meant: according to רבי, the opinions are switched.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יאשיה accepts the challenge and narrows רבי יוחנן's statement. The swap of opinions is needed only if you follow רבי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If, like רבי, a טבול יום is the same as other טומאה, then רבי מאיר's two rulings really clash, and the names in the other משנה must be switched. But someone who holds that a טבול יום is different would not need any swap. So רבי יוחנן's answer is true, but only within רבי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The opinions are switched; each view was put under the wrong sage's name
According to the view of

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: רבי יאשיה said: This is what רבי יוחנן said:
According to the words of רבי, the opinions are switched.
phrases.notes: This goes back to רבי יוחנן's answer in step 2. He is now saying it only works on רבי's view.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by agreeing that the swap depends on רבי's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of an earlier statement to one opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's swap seemed to be a general statement about how to read the sources.
steps.terutzMaskana: The swap is needed only according to רבי, who treats a טבול יום like all other טומאה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's 'the opinions are switched' answer applies only according to רבי, who makes no difference between a טבול יום and other טומאה.

steps.title: Does a handle count for הכשר or only for טומאה?
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new explanation: the תנאים argue whether a 'handle' (יד) connects things only for טומאה, or also for הכשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They argue about whether a handle counts for טומאה but not for הכשר. One sage holds that a handle counts for טומאה but not for הכשר, and the other sage holds that a handle counts for both טומאה and הכשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a whole new way to explain the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון. He does not use the idea of switching names at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that the animal works as a 'handle' for the limb that is partly cut off. The only question is what a handle does. רבי שמעון says a handle passes on טומאה but cannot pass on הכשר. רבי מאיר says it passes on both, so blood that touched the animal also makes the limb ready to become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'handle': an attached part that counts as connected to the food
Making food ready to become טמא (for example, by getting wet from certain liquids)
They argue about
One sage holds

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up טומאה and הכשר. הכשר does not make food טמא. It only makes the food able to become טמא later. רבא says the handle rule might work for one and not the other.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a new way to explain the משנה, in which both תנאים agree the animal is a handle for the limb. It also shows that a 'handle' may connect things for one purpose but not for another.

phrases.english: רבא said: About whether there is a handle for טומאה,
but there is no handle for הכשר — about this they argue.
One sage holds there is a handle for טומאה
but there is no handle for הכשר,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר יֵשׁ יָד לְטוּמְאָה וּלְהֶכְשֵׁר.
phrases.english: and the other sage holds there is a handle for טומאה and for הכשר.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: בְּיֵשׁ יָד לְטוּמְאָה, וְאֵין יָד לְהֶכְשֵׁר, קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about רבי מאיר's contradiction, רבא gives a different explanation of the משנה's dispute: both sides agree the animal is a יד, and they argue only about הכשר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what the dispute is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier explanation of the משנה made the argument about whether the animal's body counts as a יד for the limb at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees the animal is a handle for the limb. They argue only about whether a handle also passes on הכשר.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא: רבי שמעון holds a handle works for טומאה only. רבי מאיר holds a handle works for both טומאה and הכשר.

steps.title: רב פפא: the argument is about readiness before intention
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a new explanation. The תנאים argue about whether הכשר that happened before מחשבה counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: They argue about whether something can be made ready for טומאה before there was intention to use it as food.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives his own explanation of the dispute between the תנאים, different from רבא's explanation about the handle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב פפא, both sides agree that a handle connects the food. The case is one where the animal was slaughtered before the owner decided to give the meat to a gentile. So the blood of the שחיטה touched the meat before it was 'food' in the owner's mind. The question is whether that earlier contact still makes the meat ready for טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Making food ready (susceptible) to become טמא, through contact with a liquid
Intention: the owner deciding to treat something as food
They argue about

steps.confusionAlert: Two separate things are needed here. הכשר means a liquid touched the food, and מחשבה means the owner intends it as food. The question is only about their ORDER: does a הכשר that came first still count?

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
They argue about being made ready before intention.
phrases.notes: He means: did the liquid's contact count if it happened before the owner thought of this as food?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: בְּהֶכְשֵׁר קוֹדֶם מַחְשָׁבָה קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the dispute instead of רבא's handle-based explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the point of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנאים argue about whether a handle connects things for הכשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree about the handle. They argue whether הכשר before מחשבה counts.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's first teaching about village fat
steps.stepSummary: A source is brought: רבי עקיבא originally taught that fat in the villages needs מחשבה but not a new הכשר, because the שחיטה already made it ready.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי יהודה said, this is how רבי עקיבא used to teach. Fat of an animal slaughtered in the villages needs intention, but it does not need to be made ready by a liquid, because it was already made ready by the slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that this exact question, whether הכשר before מחשבה counts, was already debated. This step gives רבי עקיבא's original view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the villages, people do not usually eat the fat, so it only counts as food if someone intends to use it. רבי עקיבא first said the blood of the שחיטה already made it ready, even though that happened before the intention. So in his first view, הכשר before מחשבה does count.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat of an animal
Villages, where the fat is not usually treated as food
It was made ready for טומאה by the slaughter, meaning by the blood of the שחיטה

phrases.english: As we learned:
Rabbi Yehuda said:
This is how Rabbi Akiva used to teach:
Fat of a slaughtered animal in the villages needs intention,
but it does not need to be made ready,
since it was already made ready by the slaughter.
phrases.notes: The blood from the שחיטה is the liquid that touched the fat, even though nobody intended it as food yet.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: כָּךְ הָיָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא שׁוֹנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source showing that רב פפא's question was really debated.
steps.raayaObject: That הכשר before מחשבה is a known point of dispute
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's report of רבי עקיבא's teaching about village fat

steps.title: רבי יהודה's challenge from endives, and רבי עקיבא changes his view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה challenges רבי עקיבא from his own ruling about endives rinsed for an animal, and רבי עקיבא changes his teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said before him: You taught us, our teacher, that endives which someone picked and rinsed for an animal, and then changed his mind and decided they are for a person, need to be made ready a second time. And רבי עקיבא went back and taught like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same source, רבי יהודה points out a contradiction from רבי עקיבא's own teaching. רבי עקיבא accepts it and changes his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the endives, the water touched them when they were animal food, before they were meant for people. Yet רבי עקיבא required a second wetting, which shows that הכשר before מחשבה does NOT count. So the fat should also need a new הכשר, and רבי עקיבא agreed.

keyTerms.meaning: Endives, a leafy vegetable
He changed his mind
A second making-ready: a new contact with liquid
He retracted, went back on his earlier view

phrases.english: I said before him:
phrases.notes: "I" is רבי יהודה, still telling the story.

phrases.english: You taught us, our teacher,
endives that one picked and rinsed for an animal,
and then changed his mind about them, to use them for a person,
they need a second making-ready.

phrases.aramaic: וְחָזַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לִהְיוֹת שׁוֹנֶה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva went back to teaching like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַרְתִּי לְפָנָיו: לִמַּדְתָּנוּ רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted source with רבי יהודה's challenge and רבי עקיבא's retraction.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's first teaching that the fat needs no new הכשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the endives case, a wetting that came before the intention did not count. So the blood of the שחיטה, which also came before the intention, should not count for the fat either.

steps.title: Each תנא follows a different stage of רבי עקיבא's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא concludes: one תנא follows רבי עקיבא's original teaching, and the other follows his retraction.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds like the original teaching, and the other master holds like the retraction.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא connects the source back to the dispute in our משנה and shows where each תנא stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר follows רבי עקיבא's first view, that הכשר before מחשבה counts, so the meat is ready for טומאה. רבי שמעון follows the retraction, that it does not count. This completes רב פפא's alternative explanation of the dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: Master, meaning one of the sages in the dispute
Originally: רבי עקיבא's first teaching
The retraction: רבי עקיבא's later teaching

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's explanation: the תנאים argue about הכשר קודם מחשבה. רבי מאיר follows רבי עקיבא's first view (it counts), and רבי שמעון follows his retraction (it does not count).

phrases.english: One master holds like the original,
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר, following רבי עקיבא's first teaching.

phrases.english: and one master holds like the retraction.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר לַהּ כְּמֵעִיקָּרָא, וּמָר סָבַר לַהּ כַּחֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the two stages of רבי עקיבא's teaching to the two תנאים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute matches רבי עקיבא's two views on whether הכשר before מחשבה counts.

steps.title: The dispute is about blood wiped off between the two cuts
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא says the תנאים argue about blood that was wiped away after the first סימן was cut but before the second. The question is whether שחיטה counts from its start or only at its end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא said: they argue about a case where the blood was wiped off between the cutting of one סימן and the next. One Sage holds that שחיטה counts from beginning to end, so this is blood of slaughter. The other Sage holds that שחיטה counts only at the end, so this is just blood of a wound.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא gives a new explanation of what the two תנאים are arguing about. He points to blood that came out after the first cut and was wiped off before the second cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood of שחיטה makes food ready for טומאה (הכשר), but blood of a wound does not. If שחיטה counts from the very first cut, the early blood is דם שחיטה and gives הכשר. If שחיטה only counts when it is finished, that early blood is only דם מכה and does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the two pipes cut in שחיטה (the windpipe or the food pipe)
Was wiped off
שחיטה counts as happening all the way from the first cut to the last
Blood of slaughter, which can give הכשר
Blood of a wound, which does not give הכשר

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree a finished שחיטה is valid. The argument is only about how to label blood that came out partway through, before the second סימן was cut.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rav Ika said:
About a case where the blood was wiped off
between one סימן and the other, they disagree.
phrases.notes: He means the blood came out after the first pipe was cut and was gone before the second pipe was cut.

phrases.english: One Sage holds
that slaughter exists from beginning to end,
and so this is blood of slaughter,
and the other Sage holds
that slaughter exists only at the end,
and so this is blood of a wound.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא אָמַר: בְּנִתְקַנֵּחַ הַדָּם בֵּין סִימָן לְסִימָן קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב פפא's explanation ends in step 11, a new אמורא offers a different way to understand the מחלוקת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (blood wiped off midway) and the underlying principle (when שחיטה counts)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier explanations tied the argument to יד or to the timing of מחשבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is whether שחיטה counts from the first cut, which makes midway blood דם שחיטה, or only at the end, which makes it דם מכה.

steps.title: The dispute is whether the slaughter itself, not the blood, makes things ready
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the תנאים argue about whether the act of שחיטה makes the meat ready, rather than the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: they disagree about the rule that the שחיטה makes things ready, and not the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: One more אמורא gives yet another explanation of the מחלוקת. He says the question is what actually gives הכשר: the שחיטה itself or the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view says the act of שחיטה readies the meat because it permits it to be eaten. A limb that stays forbidden is not readied by the שחיטה, and on this view the blood does not count. The other view says the blood of שחיטה does give הכשר, so the limb that touched it becomes ready.

keyTerms.meaning: The act of slaughter itself makes the meat ready to become טמא
Making food able to become טמא, usually through contact with certain liquids

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
About the rule that slaughter makes things ready
and not the blood, they disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: בִּשְׁחִיטָה מַכְשֶׁרֶת וְלֹא דָּם קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is another alternative explanation, given right after רב אחא's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifting the source of הכשר from the blood to the act of שחיטה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument depended on how midway blood is labeled.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is whether blood of שחיטה gives הכשר, or only the שחיטה itself does, which would leave out a limb that stays forbidden.

steps.title: Can a living animal act as a handle for its limb?
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks whether an animal, while still alive, can act as a יד that passes טומאה to its partly cut-off limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה asked: an animal during its lifetime, can it become a handle for the limb?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new question. רבה asks whether the יד idea from earlier still works while the animal is alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the animal's body was treated as a יד for its hanging limb. A living animal itself cannot become טמא as food, but the hanging limb might. רבה asks whether the living body can still act as a handle to pass טומאה to the limb.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked a question that he was unsure about
A handle, a connected part that passes טומאה to the main food
A limb, here one that is partly cut off and hanging
During its lifetime, while still alive

phrases.english: Rabbah asked:
An animal during its lifetime,
what is the law: does it become a handle for the limb?
phrases.notes: This builds on רבה's explanation on the previous amud: for רבי מאיר, the animal's body counts as a יד for its limb.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבָּה: בְּהֵמָה בְּחַיֶּיהָ, מַהוּ שֶׁתֵּעָשֶׂה יָד לְאֵבֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the list of explanations, the גמרא opens a new question built on the יד idea.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a living animal's body counts as a יד for its partly cut-off limb, so that it passes טומאה to the limb.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends רבה's question with תיקו, meaning it stays open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says it has no answer to רבה's question, so it is left open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No proof is found either way. We do not know whether a living animal acts as a יד for its limb.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question stays without an answer

steps.whatToRemember: There are several explanations of the מחלוקת about the hanging limb: יד (רבא), הכשר before מחשבה (רב פפא), blood wiped off between the סימנים (רב אחא), and שחיטה versus blood (רב אשי). Whether a living animal is a יד for its limb stays a תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רבה's question from step 14 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It stays undecided whether a living animal serves as a יד for its partly cut-off limb.

steps.title: A cucumber that grew out of its flowerpot becomes pure
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a משנה: a cucumber planted in a flowerpot that grew beyond the pot's edge is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The Sages taught that if someone planted a cucumber in a flowerpot, and it grew until it stuck out past the edge of the pot, it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is quoting a משנה as background. He is setting up a new question that is similar to רבה's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plant in a flowerpot can count as detached from the ground, so it can be טמא like food. Once the cucumber grows out over the ground, this first opinion says the whole cucumber counts as attached, so it becomes טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: A cucumber
A flowerpot
Pure; not able to pass on טומאה

phrases.english: Abaye said: Behold, they said:
phrases.notes: He is quoting a משנה in מסכת עוקצין.

phrases.english: A cucumber that one planted in a flowerpot
and it grew and went out beyond the flowerpot
is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבה's question stayed open, אביי brings a similar case from a משנה about plants.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cucumber in a flowerpot that grew out beyond the pot becomes טהור.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: each part keeps its own status
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees: the impure part stays impure and the pure part stays pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: Why should it become pure? Rather, the part that was impure stays impure, and the part that is pure stays pure.
steps.whatsHappening: This is still part of the משנה אביי is quoting. רבי שמעון argues with the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון does not accept that the part growing outside makes the whole cucumber pure. In his view, one cucumber can have two statuses at the same time: the part inside the pot stays טמא, and the part outside is טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: What is its nature? Here it means: why should it change?
Ritual impurity
Ritual purity

steps.whyThisMatters: אביי's coming question only works according to רבי שמעון, because only he says one cucumber has a טמא part and a טהור part.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
But what is its nature to become pure?
Rather, the impure part stays in its impurity,
and the pure part stays in its purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: וְכִי מָה טִיבָהּ לְטַהֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the second opinion in the same משנה. It argues with the תנא קמא of step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The part inside the pot stays טמא and the part outside stays טהור.

steps.title: Can the outside part act as a handle for the inside part?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks, according to רבי שמעון, whether the pure outside part works as a יד that brings טומאה to the part inside the pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked: Can one part become a handle for the other part?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks his question based on רבי שמעון's view. It is like רבה's question about the living animal and its limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a יד passes טומאה to the food it is attached to. Here the outside part is connected to the ground, so it is in a different state from the inside part. אביי wants to know if it can still serve as a יד for the inside part.

keyTerms.meaning: A handle: a part attached to food that can pass טומאה to it
Its partner; here, the other part of the same cucumber

phrases.english: Abaye asked:
What is the law: can it become a handle for its counterpart?
phrases.notes: The outside part of the cucumber would be the handle, and the inside part would be its counterpart.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי אַבָּיֵי: מַהוּ שֶׁתֵּעָשֶׂה יָד לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי שמעון's view from step 17 and is similar to רבה's question in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a part in a different state, connected to the ground, can serve as a יד that passes טומאה to the rest of the cucumber.

steps.title: אביי's question stays open
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends אביי's question with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not answer אביי's question and leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבה's question before it, this one has no answer. Both questions ask whether something in a different state from the main food can act as its יד.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבה's living animal question and אביי's cucumber question end in תיקו. The גמרא does not decide whether a 'handle' in a different state can pass טומאה.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the question asked in step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no answer to whether the outside part of the cucumber acts as a יד for the inside part.

steps.title: Bowing to half a gourd forbids that half
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes a ruling that one who bows down to half a gourd makes it forbidden, and he begins to ask a question.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: The Sages taught that someone who bows down to half a gourd makes it forbidden. רבי ירמיה asked:
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה quotes a ruling about עבודה זרה as background. He is setting up his own question, which continues after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling shows that one part of a plant can be forbidden while the rest stays permitted. This is like רבי שמעון's idea that one cucumber can have two different statuses, and רבי ירמיה will build his question on it.

keyTerms.meaning: One who bows down, here as worship of an idol
A gourd
He made it forbidden (no benefit allowed)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: Behold, they said:
One who bows down to half a gourd has made it forbidden.
phrases.notes: Only the half he bowed to becomes forbidden, not the whole gourd.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ הַמִּשְׁתַּחֲוֶה לַחֲצִי דַלַּעַת אֲסָרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, similar question about one part of a plant being treated differently from the rest. This follows the idea of רבי שמעון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bowing down to half a gourd makes that half forbidden.
